title: perf-benchmarking-sync-2026-06-16
content:
Performance & benchmarking sync - 2026-06-16

Attendees: Asha Patel (owner), Miguel Santos, Li Wei, Samantha Green, Devon Clarke
Apologies: N/A

TL;DR:
- Canary runs from 2026-06-15 -> 2026-06-16 show a noticeable latency regression for small-batch low-latency configs and throughput drop on A100 instances under heavy batching. p95 up ~38% for short-context gen path; tokens/sec down ~22% for batched long-context runs.
- Root cause narrowed to kernel-selection fallback introduced by the kv-cache serialization fix (PR #1427) when batch size > 8 on quantized 4-bit execution path.
- Immediate mitigations: revert batching-scheduler tweak in canary, pin kernel preference to previous selector for affected models. Longer-term: add unit tests and integration perf-run in CI to catch this pattern.

Observations / Data (selected):
- Baseline (2026-06-09 run, before PR 1427):
  - model: redwood-13b-q4_0
  - nodes: a100-80gb (n1-standard)
  - config: low-latency (max_batch=4, async=false)
  - p50: 42 ms, p95: 110 ms, p99: 180 ms, throughput: 1250 tokens/s (aggregate)

- Canary (2026-06-15, after PR 1427 merged):
  - same model/config
  - p50: 46 ms (+9%), p95: 151 ms (+37%), p99: 260 ms (+44%), throughput: 980 tokens/s (-22%)

- Long-context (32k) batched runs (max_batch=32, kv-cache warm):
  - Baseline throughput: 720 tokens/s
  - Canary throughput: 560 tokens/s (-22%)
  - Observed p99 spikes to 1.2s on node during scheduling windows (coincident with fallback to scalar FP16 kernels)

What we ran (commands / short notes):
- ./bench/run_bench.sh --model redwood-13b-q4_0 --nodes a100 --max_batch 4 --seq 1024 --tag baseline-2026-06-09
- ./bench/run_bench.sh --model redwood-13b-q4_0 --nodes a100 --max_batch 4 --seq 1024 --tag canary-2026-06-15
- perf trace captured with tools/perf-collect.sh -> saved to s3://redwood-perf/captures/2026-06-15/canary-9a3f2b1.tar.gz
- micro-bench: python tools/kernels/profile_kernels.py --model redwood-13b-q4_0 --batch 16 --seq 4096
  -> showed fallback to slower kernel id "fp16_scalar_v1" for MatMul on layer 17 when batch>=8

Root cause hypothesis (current):
- PR #1427 introduced a small change in the batching scheduler to better balance KV serialization windows. Under certain batch-size thresholds (>=8) the kernel selector fails to find the preferred vectorized FP16 matmul kernel for the quantized 4-bit path and falls back to a scalar FP16 code path that is ~2x slower for large seq lengths. This manifests as higher p95/p99 and reduced tokens/s in batched scenarios.
- Reproducer commit: 9a3f2b1 (merge of PR #1427)

Repro steps validated by Li Wei:
1) checkout 9a3f2b1, build runtime with env RUNTIME_KERNEL_DEBUG=1
2) run micro-bench profile_kernels.py with batch 16 seq 4096
3) observe kernel fallback logs: "selector: missing vector_fp16_matmul for layer 17, falling back to fp16_scalar_v1"
4) checkout pre-PR commit (8f7e4c3) -> run same micro-bench -> vector_fp16_matmul used, no slowdown.

Short-term mitigations (decided):
- Roll back the batching-scheduler tweak in canary (Miguel) - ACTION-1 (owner: Miguel Santos) - target: 2026-06-17 EOD.
- Add a temporary kernel preference override for redwood-13b-q4_0 to force vectorized FP16 kernel selection for batch >= 8 (Devon) - ACTION-2 - target: 2026-06-18 EOD.
- Add an automated perf-checker job in CI that runs a minimal micro-bench on PRs touching batching/kernels (Asha + Samantha) - ACTION-3 - target: 2026-06-23.

Longer-term work (backlog / design):
- Improve kernel selector telemetry (emit kernel_id per layer to tracing) so regressions are easier to spot in production traces. (owner: Li Wei)
- Add regression test matrix for quantized paths on A100 (batch sizes 1/4/8/16/32) to perf harness, include in nightly benchmarks. (owner: eng-performing-team)
- Revisit batching scheduler heuristics to avoid oscillation between serialization windows and kernel selection boundaries. (owner: perf-working-group)

Notes / discussion highlights:
- Samantha: suggested we may be able to detect this class of fallback by adding a cheap kernel-availability probe at model load time; if probe fails, mark model variant as degraded and route to fallback model variant. This buys time while we fix the selector.
- Miguel: emphasized we need to be careful with hotfixes that change scheduling behavior; prefer kernel-preference override first to confirm causality.
- Li: logs show that fallback happens deterministically when batch >= 8 and seq >= 1024, so we can write a focused unit test that triggers the selector path.

Action items (recap):
- ACTION-1: Revert batching-scheduler tweak in canary -> Miguel Santos -> due 2026-06-17 EOD -> update PR revert link in this doc when done.
- ACTION-2: Kernel preference override for redwood-13b-q4_0 (force vector_fp16_matmul) -> Devon Clarke -> due 2026-06-18 EOD -> test results posted to slack thread.
- ACTION-3: CI perf-checker for batching/kernel changes -> Asha Patel + Samantha Green -> due 2026-06-23 -> include micro-bench script and baseline thresholds.
- ACTION-4: Kernel selector telemetry design doc -> Li Wei -> draft due 2026-06-24 -> Confluence page link when ready.

Next sync: 2026-06-18 10:00 PT (ad-hoc if rollback happens earlier).

Attachments / artifacts: perf captures, micro-bench logs, PR #1427 diff, JIRA INF-7892 (performance regression). Links above.

Notes to self: follow up with infra on whether any GPU driver updates coincide with canary runs (unlikely but check driver logs on nodes). Also cross-check recent rollout to Dedicated customers for similar telemetry (customer-facing incidents would need immediate contact).

End of notes.
